answer: Resist clones by issuing one carved token per identity. The registry photographs a walnut blank's grain, hashes it, and assigns it to a single applicant, who carves a registry-chosen sonnet into it line by line, staining each line umber and photographing it before the next line is revealed, so carving runs in strict order. A copied token fails the grain hash, and no blank serves two holders. One token costs $240 in blank, stain, and inspection plus 25 hours of carving; 10,000 fakes need 10,000 blanks, $2,400,000, and 250,000 hours, and bulk buying creates no second grain.
